task.description: Gate ELIXIR-DEV's REQ-205 implementation (Letflow.Simulation.Seed/Runner, test-support only) against docs/agents/instructions/security-invariants.md INV-1..INV-8 before REVIEWER's idiom/AC7-dependency-signoff pass.

result.scope_test_verdict: Gate genuinely applies, but only narrowly. Per security-reviewer.md's scope test, none of the five bullet triggers fire in their literal production-code sense (no lib/letflow/ diff except mix.exs's test-only dep addition; git diff main...HEAD -- lib/ priv/repo/migrations/ shows only lib/letflow/design/req205-simulation-harness-foundation.md, a doc, changed). However this test-support code EXERCISES real tenant-provisioning (Letflow.TenantOnboarding.provision_and_migrate/1), real identity/credential paths (Letflow.Identity.create_tenant/1, create_user/2, create_token/3), and dispatches real HTTP through Letflow.Router.call/2 -- i.e. it is a genuine, if test-only, tenant-data path in the sense INV-1's and INV-4's rules care about (does scoping get derived correctly at the point these paths are exercised; are secrets ever mishandled). Agreeing with ELIXIR-DEV's own routing note: reviewed under INV-1 and INV-4, which are the two invariants whose mechanism this code actually touches. INV-2/INV-3/INV-5/INV-9 do not apply (no API response-shaping, no scripting sandbox, no lookup-by-ID endpoint being added, no outbound tenant-controlled URL). INV-6 applies as the meta-invariant this handoff itself satisfies. INV-7/INV-8 checked for completeness.

invariant_assessment.INV-1: APPLIES (test-support code exercising tenant provisioning/schema-scoping). SATISFIED. Verified all three sub-checks from security-invariants.md's How-to-verify: (a) every Letflow.Identity/Letflow.Definitions/Letflow.Engine/Letflow.Instances/Letflow.Tasks/Letflow.Audit call in seed.ex and runner.ex passes an explicit prefix: derived value, never omitted, never defaulting to public schema -- confirmed by reading every call site in test/support/simulation/seed.ex (seed_company/create_company has no prefix arg because tenant/onboarding rows are intentionally public-schema per Letflow.TenantProvisioning's own design -- correct, matches production Identity.create_tenant/1's own contract) and test/support/simulation/runner.ex (every Definitions/Engine/Instances/Tasks/Audit call carries prefix: prefix or opts: [prefix: ...]). (b) No new migration in this diff (git diff --stat confirms no priv/repo/migrations/ changes) -- N/A, correctly so. (c) The critical check: schema_name!/1 (seed.ex line 366-370) and tenant_prefix!/1 (runner.ex line 552-562) both derive the tenant's Postgres schema/prefix from Letflow.TenantProvisioning.schema_name_for_tenant/1 (resolved from the tenant's own id, itself sourced from a just-created or looked-up Tenant record) -- never from a caller-supplied literal string threaded in from fixture YAML or scenario args. The scenario's expected_outcome/precondition 'prefix' field (e.g. args["prefix"]) IS caller/test-author-supplied, but this is test-harness plumbing analogous to a test author picking which tenant's DB to assert against in any other test in this suite, not a production caller-supplied value disagreeing with the schema the data was written into -- the actual WRITE path (seed.ex) never accepts a caller-supplied prefix, only derives one. This is exactly the distinction 0003's addendum (INV-1's own reference) protects against, and it holds here.
invariant_assessment.INV-4: APPLIES (real credential issuance exercised in test setup). SATISFIED. Checked test/letflow/simulation/runner_test.exs's setup/0: Identity.create_token/3 is called for real (line 67-68), and the returned plaintext token is held only in a local variable / test context map (%{"token" => plaintext, ...}), passed directly into the Scenario struct's actors field in-memory, used once as a Bearer header value, and never logged, never written to a file, never serialised into any handoff or report artifact. grep -rniE for hardcoded password/secret/client_secret/token literals across test/support/simulation/, test/fixtures/simulation/, test/letflow/simulation/ returned zero hits -- no hardcoded credentials in Seed/Runner or the 12 fixture YAML files (fixture content is non-secret business data: slugs, display names, org-structure people/groups, process graphs). grep for System.get_env in the new files returned zero hits, which is correct here since no config-sourced secret is needed by this module (it mints its own ephemeral test tokens via the real create_token/3 API, the same idiom used elsewhere in this suite).
invariant_assessment.INV-2: NOT-APPLICABLE. No API response-shaping/field-authorisation code added; Runner consumes raw response bodies for template substitution and outcome verification, it does not implement or change any server-side response serialisation path.
invariant_assessment.INV-3: NOT-APPLICABLE. No Lua/WASM/tenant-authored-script execution path touched; Runner's :custom precondition dispatch is a closed, named-function-clause registry (custom_predicate/1, only "always_true" defined) with no arbitrary code execution from YAML content, correctly noted in the module's own comment as deliberately not data-driven.
invariant_assessment.INV-5: NOT-APPLICABLE. No new lookup-by-ID endpoint added; Instances.get_by_id/2 and Tasks.get_task/2 are pre-existing production functions being called from a test harness, not new endpoints.
invariant_assessment.INV-6: APPLIES as the meta-invariant this handoff itself discharges -- this document is the explicit per-invariant statement of applicability and satisfaction the meta-invariant requires.
invariant_assessment.INV-7: NOT-APPLICABLE / clean. grep -rn "Repo.query" across the diff's files: runner_test.exs's teardown/1 uses Repo.query!(~s(DROP SCHEMA IF EXISTS "#{schema_name}" CASCADE)) -- schema_name here is not tenant/user-controlled input, it is the value just returned by TenantProvisioning.schema_name_for_tenant/1 for a tenant this same test created moments earlier (a generated, provisioning-owned identifier, not attacker-reachable), and this exact idiom (dynamic schema name in a DROP SCHEMA statement) is already the established pattern this repo's other tenant-provisioning tests use for teardown, per ELIXIR-DEV's own convention citation. No bind-parameterizable alternative exists for a DROP SCHEMA statement (identifiers cannot be bind params in Postgres), and the identifier's provenance is trusted, so this is not an INV-7 violation.
invariant_assessment.INV-8: NOT-APPLICABLE / clean. This is test-support code, not a shared production process -- a crash here fails the test run, it does not take down other tenants' in-flight work (INV-8's actual harm model). Spot-checked for the grep pattern anyway; no bare `{:ok, x} =` matches against realistically-failing external calls found in seed.ex/runner.ex (all external calls go through `with`/`case` and produce explicit {:error, _} branches per the moduledoc's own idempotency-and-race documentation).
invariant_assessment.INV-9: NOT-APPLICABLE. No outbound HTTP request to a tenant-controlled external URL; Letflow.Router.call/2 is an in-process Plug dispatch to Letflow's own router, not an outbound :httpc/webhook call.

additional_checks.yaml_elixir_dependency: {:yaml_elixir, "~> 2.11", only: :test} in mix.exs, resolved to 2.12.2 in mix.lock, depends only on :yamerl (also hexpm). No known CVEs found for yaml_elixir/yamerl as of this review; both are long-standing, widely-used Elixir/Erlang YAML libraries. Scope is only: :test in mix.exs (confirmed by direct read) so it never ships in a :prod release, and elixirc_paths(:test) already includes "test/support" (mix.exs line 20-21, pre-existing, no change needed) -- both AC7-adjacent scoping claims in ELIXIR-DEV's handoff are confirmed correct by direct inspection, not merely trusted. REVIEWER still owes the formal AC7 sign-off per the requirement's own acceptance criterion; this review only confirms the scoping facts REVIEWER's sign-off will rely on.
additional_checks.no_production_code_touched: git diff main...HEAD --stat -- lib/ priv/repo/migrations/ shows exactly one file changed under lib/: lib/letflow/design/req205-simulation-harness-foundation.md (a design doc, not code). No route, controller, context module, or migration under lib/letflow/ or priv/repo/migrations/ was modified. All 25 other changed files are under test/, handoffs/, or mix.exs/mix.lock.
additional_checks.auth_pipeline_not_bypassed: Letflow.Simulation.Runner.dispatch_api_step/4 builds a Plug.Test conn with real Authorization: Bearer <plaintext-token> and x-tenant-slug headers and calls Letflow.Router.call(request_conn, @router_opts) -- the same real Letflow.Router used in production, which per lib/letflow/router.ex's own comments routes non-explicitly-public paths through Letflow.Plugs.AuthPipeline with no bypass. Confirmed no test-only auth shortcut, mock plug, or header injection that skips AuthPipeline exists anywhere in runner.ex. This pattern is safe to exist in test-support code and would not mask a real security gap if copied elsewhere, since it exercises the real pipeline rather than substituting for it.

result.note_on_elixir_dev_disclosure: ELIXIR-DEV's honest disclosure that R-Co source was unreachable and synthetic fixtures were substituted (AC1's literal 'ported from R-Co' content requirement not met) is a requirement-completeness/AC-satisfaction question for RELEASE-VALIDATOR/ORCH, not a security concern -- the synthetic fixtures contain no secrets and exercise the identical code paths real fixtures would, so this disposition does not change the security verdict. Not re-litigated here; flagged only for completeness of this handoff's record.

next_action: Route to REVIEWER for idiom/supervision/scope-creep review and the formal AC7 (yaml_elixir dependency) sign-off per WF-02 Step 2d.
